project_profile.composition: Activity with an app-owned content view and a custom overlay View for glass controls
project_profile.minimum_target: Must be read from Gradle; supported devices include more than one Android API/GPU capability tier
project_profile.backdrop_access: The app owns the content view, but a safe and current backdrop capture path has not yet been verified
project_profile.graphics: Hardware acceleration is enabled; API-gated effects and OpenGL ES capabilities still require runtime/minimum-target checks

task: Create a refractive media-control capsule with a circular play lens and a search-like lobe that expands from and reconnects with the capsule.
must_discover: Gradle minSdk/targetSdk, Java source/target compatibility, and existing build tasks
View hierarchy, owner of the backdrop, window compositing, and custom drawing lifecycle
hardware acceleration and API-gated native visual-effect availability
OpenGL ES/shader support on the minimum device range, if a shader path is considered
touch, accessibility semantics, focus, and reduced-motion settings
must_consider: native View/material and custom drawing options before introducing a new rendering surface
an app-owned offscreen or GPU path only if capture, lifecycle, and compositing can be validated
runtime/API/GPU gates for optional rendering features
semantic Android controls and hit regions independent from the deforming visual mask
a stable lower-tier fallback for unsupported devices
must_not_assume: all Android API levels expose the same blur or backdrop effects
hardware acceleration implies arbitrary live backdrop sampling
OpenGL ES 3 support exists on every supported device
a shader overlay can be added without checking View/Surface z-order and lifecycle
a blurred surface is true refraction

workflow.required_output: Java/XML project, Gradle targets, minimum API, View/composition ownership, graphics facilities, and build baseline
capsule and circular-lens shapes, connected-lobe transition, backdrop criteria, and stable media-control semantics
compare native View/compositor, custom drawing, gated GPU path, hybrid overlay, and fallback
small Java/View integration, lifecycle-owned resources, semantic controls, API/GPU gates, and fallback
incremental shape, optical layers, input/motion state, and crisp accessible controls
Gradle build/tests, minimum/API branches, device/runtime smoke test, screenshots, touch/focus, reduced motion, and performance
changed files, real test results, fidelity tier, unsupported device branches, and evidence

acceptance: The minimum target is discovered rather than guessed
Native and GPU approaches are compared against actual backdrop/compositor access
No API or GLES capability is claimed without a gate or test
Fallback and fidelity tier are explicit for lower-capability devices
